description: B.1 — Test cyFlQ-agent hypothesis #2: Vol(closure of β_p) / ℏ_q² ≟ m_p. Reads existing proton-braid closure volumes from fresh-derivation-pn-steps-A-D.witness.json (4 channel branches, β_p ∈ B_3 with 11 crossings) and divides by ℏ_q² = ((q-1)/q)².  Result: Vol/ℏ_q² ranges 10⁻⁵–10⁻³ vs m_p = 938.27 MeV — off by 8+ orders of magnitude. Hypothesis FALSIFIED with the current proton-braid representation.
interpretation: For Vol/ℏ_q² to equal m_p ≈ 938.27 MeV in natural units, the proton braid would need Vol(closure) ≈ m_p · ℏ_q² ≈ 9.21 — a substantial hyperbolic knot like 4_1 (Vol 2.03) scaled up.  The actual β_p in B_3 with 11 crossings closes to a 2-component link of tiny volume (mostly torus-like, one branch Vol ≈ 4e-6).  The hypothesis as stated requires either: (i) a fundamentally different braid representation of the proton; (ii) a different Kashaev-volume formula scaling than Vol/ℏ_q²; or (iii) accepting m_p as a genuine third calibration input.  Combined with T1.1's falsification of Δm = m_e·Σ_3, the simplest 'drop to 2-cal' route via the fresh_derivation_pn pipeline is closed.
next_steps: Test alt. functional forms: Vol·m_e/ℏ_q^k for k ∈ {1,2,3,4}; Vol-via-colored-Jones (Kashaev limit) instead of geometric Vol.

Consider whether the proton's correct representation is a HIGHER-strand braid (B_3 with quark-only crossings is the leptonic-content sketch; full hadronic content may require multi-strand resolution of dressed quarks).
If no closed form exists for m_p from (q_0, m_e), accept the 3-input framework and focus on Term 7 (A.1-4) for the binding-gap closure.
